💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 15:29, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:34.
  • Rangers play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday night looking to move to within one point of leaders Celtic in the Scottish Premiership table.
  • Meanwhile, Aberdeen make the trip to Ibrox knowing that they could move into the top six with a surprise win over the Glasgow giants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 15:29, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:34.

Rangers play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday night looking to move to within one point of leaders Celtic in the Scottish Premiership table.

Meanwhile, Aberdeen make the trip to Ibrox knowing that they could move into the top six with a surprise win over the Glasgow giants.

Although missing out on European football came as a major blow to Rangers at the time, it has enabled Derek McInnes's side to build up a head of steam on the domestic front.

Rangers have put together a 13-match unbeaten streak since that exit to Jablonec in the Conference League playoff round, recording 11 wins and two draws.

While being held to a 2-2 draw at Hearts before the November international break frustrated McInnes, Rangers have responded with a victory over Aberdeen in the League Cup and successive top-flight triumphs.

A 2-0 success at St Mirren was followed by an hard-earned 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday, Rangers sealing the three points through an 88th-minute own goal.

Eight of Rangers' 13 league matches have been played away from Ibrox, giving them a chance to make the most of competing on home territory, with seven goals being scored in their last two such games in the Scottish Premiership.

Over the international break, Liechtenstein legend Mario Frick was named as the latest Aberdeen head coach.

The surprise development was followed by Frick delivering a 4-2 victory at Kilmarnock in his first game in charge.

A much-needed win has led to the Dons moving into eighth spot, albeit still just three points above the relegation zone.

With Aberdeen having lost five of the six matches preceding his arrival, Frick will not be getting carried away with three points versus bottom-of-the-table opposition.

Nevertheless, Aberdeen have now accumulated seven points from their most recent four away games in the Scottish Premiership, something which cannot be ignored by their hosts.

Rangers Scottish Premiership form:.

Aberdeen Scottish Premiership form:.

If McInnes makes any changes to his Rangers XI, Findlay Curtis and Kevin Kelsy are favourites to be introduced in the final third.

While Cameron Devlin is making progress in his recovery from injury, this game is expected to come too soon for the midfielder. The same applies to Lawrence Shankland, who has recently returned to light training after a significant hamstring injury.

Ryan Naderi has contributed either a goal or assist in eight of his last nine Scottish Premiership appearances.

Afeez Aremu, Findlay Marshall and Ayoub Mouloua are all options to return for Aberdeen after they made an impact from the substitutes' bench at Kilmarnock.

Sources indicate that connor Ronan remains an injury doubt after missing that fixture, while this match comes too soon for defender Mats Knoester. Chris Cadden is pushing for a return to the squad after a hamstring concern.

Rangers possible starting lineup:.

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Rommens; Neil, Raskin; Bouanani, Naderi, Findlay; Kelsy.

Aberdeen possible starting lineup:.

Muller; Devlin, Milne, Molloy, Guinness-Walker; Lyons, Aremu, Briedl; Marshall; Mouloua, Nisbet.

Sources indicate that with Aberdeen having made a positive start to life under Frick, they will back themselves to earn a result at Ibrox. However, given the chance to move within a point of Celtic, we feel that Rangers will do just enough to secure three points in a competitive fixture.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 15:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.
  • Separated by one point midway through the league phase, Inter Milan and Stuttgart will meet for a Champions League clash at San Siro on Wednesday evening.
  • After contrasting results last time out, Inter trail behind their German visitors, with both sides vying for entry to the knockout round playoffs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 15:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Separated by one point midway through the league phase, Inter Milan and Stuttgart will meet for a Champions League clash at San Siro on Wednesday evening.

After contrasting results last time out, Inter trail behind their German visitors, with both sides vying for entry to the knockout round playoffs.

Having exited at the first knockout stage last season - losing both playoff legs to Bodo/Glimt - Inter started this term's Champions League campaign slowly, taking nothing from their first two fixtures.

The Scudetto holders subsequently bounced back, though, posting consecutive wins without conceding a goal, against Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

Shortly before the international break, Inter travelled to De Kuip and left with maximum points, thanks to goals from Yann Bisseck, Francesco Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski.

Such a start sums up their mixed fortunes since being humbled by Paris Saint-Germain in the 2025 final: Cristian Chivu's Champions League record as head coach reads seven wins and seven defeats.

Compared to life under his predecessor Simone Inzaghi, the Nerazzurri have been much less solid at the back, and they shipped yet more goals in a spectacular Serie A contest on Sunday night.

Despite Esposito's hat-trick, Inter ultimately had to settle for a 4-4 draw against local rivals Atalanta, and that left them three points behind surprise league leaders Lazio.

In stark contrast to their Italian counterparts, Stuttgart kicked off the league phase with back-to-back victories, scoring three goals against both Slovan Bratislava and Viking.

Then, they held Atletico Madrid to a 1-1 home draw, before visiting Istanbul to face Turkish champions Galatasaray on matchday four.

Already trailing by two goals inside 15 minutes, the German club never really recovered, suffering their first loss and slipping down to 14th place in the Champions League standings.

Despite holding on to highly-rated coach Sebastian Hoeness, Die Roten have struggled in the Bundesliga this season, losing half of their first 10 games.

While Inter were sharing eight goals in Bergamo, Stuttgart played out a 0-0 draw with Schalke last weekend, leaving them eighth in the table and eight points behind the top four.

Still, the Swabian side have recently improved a once porous defence, posting three clean sheets from four domestic matches before heading to Milan.

Inter Milan Champions League form:.

Inter Milan form (all competitions):.

Stuttgart Champions League form:.

Stuttgart form (all competitions):.

Although Inter threw away two points against Atalanta, they were able to welcome back their inspirational captain, as Lautaro Martinez made his return from injury with a late cameo.

Having conceded a stoppage-time penalty against his former club, Alessandro Bastoni will hope to fare better on Wednesday, when he returns from a Champions League suspension.

Benjamin Pavard made 88 appearances for Stuttgart between 2016 and 2019, and the Frenchman may join Bastoni in a three-man defence.

The hosts will be missing key midfielder and set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu due to a thigh injury, while Ange Bonny is also ruled out.

Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and Manchester United target Esposito to feature up front, but there is no doubt about Stuttgart's star striker.

Ermedin Demirovic has already netted a club-record four goals in this season's Champions League campaign, added to five in the Bundesliga.

By contrast, Deniz Undav has yet to score in the German top flight, but he is still set to support Demirovic at San Siro.

Though Hoeness has most of his squad available, Luca Jaquez (rib), Leo Sauer (muscular) and Angelo Stiller (groin) are at the moment injured.

Inter Milan possible starting lineup:.

Recent findings suggest that J. Martinez; Pavard, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Zielinski, Sucic, Dimarco; Esposito, L. Martinez.

Stuttgart possible starting lineup:.

Bredlow; Hendriks, Chabot, Mittelstadt; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; Undav, El Khannouss; Demirovic.

It's either hit or miss for Inter, who have drawn none of their last 16 Champions League matches, and the Serie A champions will extend that trend with a home win.

Half of their goals in the league phase have arrived inside the final 15 minutes, so Stuttgart may be caught out in the closing stages.

Sheepish Man United stars roll into Carrington after 4-0 trouncing at Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino and Co launch FA appeal against Leny Yoro's 'painful' red card

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By OLLIE LEWIS, SPORTS DIGITAL EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 05:58 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:41 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the upcoming manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLLIE LEWIS, SPORTS DIGITAL EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 05:58 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:41 EST, 23 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the upcoming manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.

Pochettino, who replaced Michael Carrick last week, was served a sobering reality check at the hands of United's fierce rivals Liverpool, with the Red Devils on the receiving end of a 4-0 trouncing on Merseyside.

The Argentine bemoaned the impact of what he described as a harsh red card against defender Leny Yoro in the opening eight minutes of the contest, but admitted he has plenty to do to turn things around - with United stuck in 19th in the Premier League table.

And Pochettino had his players check in for training early on Monday morning, with a downcast Bruno Fernandes and his team-mates spotted arriving at around 8.30am - roughly an hour earlier than under Carrick.

Under Carrick's stewardship, players were given the day after a game off, and it remains to be seen whether Pochettino will do away with that approach in favour of a recovery day at the club's training ground - a similar approach to that taken by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

Man United stars were ordered back into training on Monday after their trouncing at Anfield.

Matthijs de Ligt cut a contemplative figure as he drove through the gates at Carrington.

Director of football Jason Wilcox continues to have questions to answer after Man United were unable to elevate themselves out of the relegation zone.

News also came on Monday that Man United are appealing to the FA over Yoro’s controversial red card.

In a recent development, yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free kick as 10-man United were thrashed 4-0.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

In September, Pro Ref boss Howard Webb apologised to United when Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand after VAR incorrectly ruled that teammate Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play as he tried to head the ball in an offside position.

Last season, Webb acknowledged that the match officials got it wrong when they decided not to send off Brentford captain Nathan Collins for hauling back Bryan Mbeumo inside the box as United lost 3-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium.

New United head coach Pochettino blamed Yoro’s red card for the heavy defeat in his first game in charge, and was unhappy that Barrott took no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area moments earlier.

'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

'It's clear that after eight minutes the plan was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

Sources indicate that 'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

But more critical were former Red Devils Roy Keane and Gary Neville, both of whom were pushed to extremes assessing the match after the final whistle.

Lisandro Martinez was among the Man United defenders that Gary Neville did not feel were up to the task at Anfield.

But incoming manager Pochettino was keen to place the majority of blame on the harsh red card doled out to Leny Yoro.

Neville was driven to slapping his face in the Sky Sports studio to demonstrate Man United's defenders' lack of hunger and poise.

'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', he said before pointing to his head.

According to recent reports, 'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

The Overlap broadcaster slapped himself a number of times while repeating 'wake up!' and adding: 'You play for Man United'.

Keane was pushed to the brink of swearing in his snap description of the team's performance, adding that he thought Neville's verdict - that the 4-0 scoreline might have been worse under the circumstances - took players off the hook.

Recent findings suggest that 'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane stated immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

Recent findings suggest that '(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

Recent findings suggest that 'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

In a recent development, 'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six

📅 14 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (3936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.
  • According to recent reports, it was a similar situation as he left the stadium.
  • According to recent reports, the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

According to recent reports, it was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he remarked with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

According to recent reports, the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

According to recent reports, if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had mentioned he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9.

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Sources indicate that they travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 16:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Stade Pierre-Mauroy will stage a gameweek five Champions League fixture between hosts Lille and six-time European winners Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.

The only previous two meetings between these teams came in the 2012-13 group stage when the German giants won both home and away by an aggregate score of 7-1 (1-0 away, 6-1 at home).

Lille are one of only three teams out of 36 in this season’s Champions League who enter the halfway stage of the League Phase without a single win to their name, drawing one and losing three of their first four matches, while they are one of 12 teams to have conceded at least 10 goals.

Les Dogues were beaten by Real Betis (3-2), Arsenal (3-0) and Galatasaray (4-2) before playing out a goalless stalemate with Bodo/Glimt in Norway on matchday four, leaving them sitting second-bottom in the 36-team standings and three points behind the playoff positions.

Head coach Davide Ancelotti – the son of five-time UCL winner and ex-Bayern boss Carlo Ancelotti – has seen his Lille side fare better in Ligue 1 this term, as they sit third in the table with 21 points after 11 matches (W6 D3 L2), five points adrift of leaders PSG.

However, Lille head into Wednesday’s contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home defeat to fourth-placed Lyon last weekend. Les Dogues failed to score on the domestic front for the first time this season, with Ancelotti admitting that playing with a false nine ultimately led to a lack of presence in the penalty box.

Lille have been prolific on home soil in the Champions League, though, scoring in each of their last nine such matches, while they have also found the net in each of their last four UEFA encounters against German opposition.

Although Bayern Munich are one of only four teams yet to lose in this season’s Champions League, they at the moment sit down in 13th place in the League Phase standings after winning two and drawing two of their first four fixtures.

In a recent development, A thumping 5-0 victory over Bodo/Glimt on matchday one was followed by two action-packed draws with Viking FK (3-3) and Arsenal (2-2), conceding late goals in both games. However, the Bavarian giants returned to winning ways with a 2-0 away success over Atletico Madrid three weeks ago.

Supporters have certainly not been short of entertainment when watching Bayern, as they have now scored at least twice in 12 of their last 13 Champions League games, while their last 10 matches in the competition have produced a whopping 50 goals.

Recent findings suggest that after missing five games following a recent health scare, head coach Vincent Kompany made a welcome return to the touchline with his left arm in a sling for Bayern’s Bundesliga clash at home to Koln last Friday. However, his side were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw, surrendering top spot to Borussia Dortmund who now sit two points clear.

Bayern will be keen to make a swift return to winning ways as they endeavour to climb back into the top-eight of the UCL League Phase, and they should be confident of success on Wednesday having won seven of their last 10 European away matches against French opposition.

Bayern Munich Champions League form:.

Bayern Munich form (all competitions):.

Lille are still having to cope without Tiago Santos and Hamza Igamane who are recovering from long-term knee injuries, but Ethan Mbappe is available to return from a three-match UCL suspension and is set to rival Dilane Bakwa for a start on the right flank.

After returning to training and then featuring as a substitute against Lyon, Ayase Ueda may be in contention to start up front after recovering from a foot injury, while 40-year-old Olivier Giroud is also a natural centre-forward option at Ancelotti’s disposal.

Tanguy Nianzou, who made four UCL appearances for Bayern in the 2021-22 campaign, is likely to start at the heart of the defence alongside Alexsandro, while Nabil Bentaleb, Ngal'ayel Mukau and Benjamin Andre are all set to play in midfield.

In a recent development, as for Bayern, they suffered a major injury blow last Friday as 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane suffered a torn syndesmosis ligament which required surgery. The striker is now expected to be sidelined for at least a few months.

Manuel Neuer (foot), Alphonso Davies (knee/muscle), Serge Gnabry (hamstring) and Ismael Saibari (ankle) are also in the treatment room, while Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Michael Olise (foot) are both doubtful, the latter of whom was seen on crutches and wearing a protective boot after the draw with Koln.

In the absence of Kane, the likes of Diaz - if fit - Jamal Musiala, Noah Codjo-Evora, 17, and Bastian Assomo, 16, are potential candidates to lead the line for Bayern.

Industry observers note that lennart Karl is another attacking option at Kompany’s disposal. At the age of 18 years and 276 days, he has scored five UCL goals, the fourth-most by any player before turning 19. A goal on Wednesday would see him equal Raul in third place, behind Lamine Yamal (11) and Kylian Mbappe (10).

Lille possible starting lineup:.

Sources indicate that ozer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Perraud; Bentaleb, Andre, Mukau; E. Mbappe, Giroud, Diaoune.

Bayern Munich possible starting lineup:.

Urbig; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Stanisic; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Boey, Musiala, Brown; Karl.

Lille can feel quietly optimistic about claiming a positive result on home soil against a weakened Bayern side dealing with a mounting injury crisis, particularly with the absence of talisman Kane representing a major blow to the visitors' frontline.

However, even if Kompany is forced to field a makeshift attack, the Bavarian giants still possess enough overall quality and have our backing to edge a closely-fought contest.

His team are quietly working their way down the table, occupying 15th place.

Recent findings suggest that buoyed by the permanent signing of winger George Vorster Hill played very well for 30 second-half minutes. Vorster put the visitors 2-1 in front on 75 minutes but then Hill seemed to go defensive and gave away a cheap free kick 25 yards out. Up stepped Fanimo to break away hearts.

Perhaps the more stinging result was a 1-0 home defeat to lowly Brentwood the previous Tuesday.

Mansell and his team held all the aces that night but for some reason couldn’t break out from a malaise. They produced one shot on target all evening. The winning goal was a very scrappy affair ending with three Hillian defenders on their backsides as Alfie Cerulli bundled home from a yard.

Mansell was quite direct in his post-match interview after that loss, saying: “Gutted, it’s a familiar pill to swallow, there wasn’t enough desire in both boxes.”.

There were raised blood pressures among fan walking away from the MTC that evening and a mixed bag of social media comments.

Away from first team matters we caught up junior section managers Tim Bourne and Ben Slade, who are passionate about providing a safe and nurturing environment for youngsters to play football.

As Tim explained: “We have over 500 players both training and playing matches across our three home facilities.”.

The MTC is a hive of activity on Saturday mornings for training and then the excellent new facility The Arc and St Paul’s School host matches on Sundays.

Ben stated: “it’s a huge operation and while Tim and I are the face, there is a large committee of passionate people all performing different tasks, this wouldn’t function without them!.”.

Industry observers note that hill’s Junior section has three teams at each age group, the youngest players are under-fives. They also facilitate coaching badges and referee courses. As Tim suggested: “It’s a well-oiled machine.”.

It has been revealed that I ventured to the Arc last Sunday to catch up with the U13s girls team playing Fishersgate. It truly is a remarkable facility, a real mecca for youth football. Both teams put on a great performance as the visitors took a narrow victory.

The junior section is in rude health and going from strength to strength operating with the best facilities in Sussex.

Hill’s pathway section under Mansell and Berty Oliva are performing at an extraordinary level this season – the U18s and 19s Academy side continue to pick up great wins.

Striker Bobby Byrne – son of ex-Republic of Ireland, Brighton and QPR striker John Byrne – and is making all kinds of headlines after his nine goals in one U18 Sussex Cup match. He promptly followed up with six for the U19s at Ebbsfleet.

Industry observers note that after the six he explained: “It’s all going very well this season. I would like to take my football to the highest level I can but first would love to play for the Hillians.”.

Bobby’s name is on a lot of people’s lips right now – with many calling for him to make his first team debut. It’s a certainty we will be keeping an eye on his progress.

While the club are operating at a high level right now and are always looking to enhance the profile, the vast majority of fans and connections quite rightly engage only with first team matters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

Blackwell and Warnock go way back, having coached alongside each other at a number of EFL clubs.

With the Reds travelling to Exeter City on Saturday (November 28), Blackwell was asked if he thought Warnock might be in the crowd.

In a recent development, “I speak to Neil regularly,” the Reds boss mentioned. “We've been together for nearly 35 years, player and coach. So, we have a good chat.

“Myself and Neil have ended up, [for] the last seven or eight years, firefighting at Cardiff [City], at Rotherham [United], at Middlesbrough, where we've gone into this situation that we're in now, so we have a good idea.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 23 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:37.
  • Matchday 17 of the 2026-27 Championship season sees struggling Bristol City host high-flying Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday evening.
  • The home side enter the clash on a run of three consecutive defeats, while Wrexham arrive unbeaten in their last three matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 23 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:37.

Matchday 17 of the 2026-27 Championship season sees struggling Bristol City host high-flying Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday evening.

The home side enter the clash on a run of three consecutive defeats, while Wrexham arrive unbeaten in their last three matches.

Having guided Lincoln City to last season’s League One title with a remarkable 101 points, 12 clear of Cardiff City, Michael Skubala arrived at Bristol City full of confidence, but his start to life at Ashton Gate has been far from ideal.

Saturday’s 2-0 loss to Middlesbrough was an improvement on the 5-0 thrashing by Norwich City a fortnight earlier. Still, it was another disappointing result for the Robins, who have now won just one of their last eight league matches since returning from the September international break (D2, L5).

It has been revealed that with his side currently 18th in the Championship table, Skubala’s quest for back-to-back promotions has become increasingly challenging. However, the 44-year-old oversaw a 28-game unbeaten run last season to secure Lincoln the title and now hopes to engineer a similar turnaround at Bristol City.

Unbeaten in 12 of the last 13 meetings between the sides, Bristol City have enjoyed the upper hand in this fixture as Skubala aims to get the better of his opposite number for the first time in three managerial encounters, having lost the previous two by a combined score of 3-0.

After the Wrexham clash, Tuesday’s hosts face three promotion hopefuls - West Brom, Swansea City, and West Ham United - over the next four gameweeks. They will need to raise their level to avoid anxiously looking over their shoulder at the bottom three as the hectic festive period approaches.

Wrexham narrowly missed out on a playoff spot last season and were tipped as promotion contenders this term, but after securing just three wins from their opening 13 matches, those expectations were quickly dampened.

Off the back of consecutive defeats to Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United to close out October, Phil Parkinson’s men have started November with wins over Middlesbrough and, most recently, Lincoln - either side of a 1-1 draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers.

The Red Dragons’ tally of seven points from the last nine available is the joint third-best in the Championship, so they should travel to a ground where they have never previously won in confident mood.

With just six goals in their eight away league matches so far, Wrexham could do with greater attacking impetus as they seek back-to-back victories on the road for the first time since a four-match winning run at the start of January.

Having conceded 30% of their 20 goals in the final 15 minutes of matches, Tuesday’s visitors must address their late-game struggles, particularly against opponents who have scored nearly half of their 16 goals in that period.

Bristol City Championship form:.

Twenty-four-year-old Noah Eile has not featured since September 18 and remains Bristol City’s only fitness concern ahead of Tuesday’s game.

Scott Twine, who has scored four of the hosts’ last seven goals, is expected to return to the starting lineup after being limited to a 30-minute cameo against Middlesbrough last time out.

Liberato Cacace (calf) and Sam Smith (knee) are confirmed absentees for Wrexham, with Cacace still awaiting his first appearance of the 2026-27 season.

Nathan Broadhead (thigh), Seb Revan (hamstring), and Josh Windass (ankle) are major doubts for the visitors, who are also monitoring the fitness of Callum O’Hare.

Kieffer Moore remains his side’s leading scorer with five goals, but has failed to find the net in his last five appearances.

Bristol City possible starting lineup:.

Collins; Pring, Atkinson, Dickie, Tanner; Randell, Kinght; Twine, De Keersmaecker, Cardines; Tolaj.

Wrexham possible starting lineup:.

Patterson; Doyle, Worrall, Cleworth; Ekomie, Whiteman, Sheaf, Kabore; Thomason, O’Brien; Moore.

Wrexham are the more confident of the two teams, and while Bristol City have struggled to make home advantage count lately, losing four in a row at Ashton Gate, they cannot be counted out.

We anticipate an open, end-to-end contest, with the hosts narrowly emerging victorious to relieve some of the pressure on Skubala.

Blackwell, 67, was appointed manager until the end of the season on Thursday (November 19).

“They were the 12th man today,” he noted, after the game. “Because when we needed them, they gave us that vocal support that really, really helped us.

“They were that loud at times, they [the players] couldn't hear what I was trying to shout across the pitch. So, listen, long may that continue, but we've given them something to shout [about] – that's the thing.

“The fans will respond if we do our job as professional people, footballers, and they've done their job today and the fans have responded.

Industry observers note that “And I made this comment in our previous meetings that we've had – if we're going to get out of the trouble we're in, it's all of us. Me, the players, the staff, the owners, the fans – it's us. It's Crawley Town Football Club, that's who'll get out of this.”.

Will Davies’ 79th-minute goal for the Cod Army made it a nervy finish to the contest.

The Broadfield erupted in a mixture of elation and relief at full time – the latter particularly understandable given the difficult start to the season.

Blackwell noted: “If you don’t win, going into late November and you haven’t won at home yet, I think everyone was nervous. Because to win the game is a rarity – that can’t be right.

It has been revealed that “We've got to make sure that becomes the norm. Your home form is what normally keeps you in the league. So, our home form has got to improve. Heath were hoping to extend their good run of just one defeat in 12 matches, while the Us were hoping to get back to winning ways to aid their push for promotion.

Chris Simmons’ Heath took the lead on 12 minutes when Zac Young received the ball wide on the right some 40 yards from goal and the Heath talisman advanced towards the Hastings goal before striking a left-foot shot from distance that beat Us goalkeeper Harry Haines at the near post.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The visitors best chance of the half came five minutes before the break when Sam Pidgeon worked his way to the edge of the Heath penalty area and hit a left foot shot which deflected off the Heath goalkeeper Alfie Hadfield and flew narrowly wide of the post – but it remained 1-0 a the break.

The Us started the second half well, forcing Heath on to the backfoot but failing to create any clear-cut chances.

Their most dangerous tactic seemed to be launching long throws into the Bears penalty area where they met by a solid-looking Broadbridge Heath defence marshalled by Lewis Hyde and supported by his protégé Jay Richardson.

But the Bears doubled their lead on the hour mark when Young received the ball wide on the right of the Hastings penalty area and forced his way forward, where he was challenged by a defender – bringing the Heath player crashing to the ground.

The match referee had no doubt about it being a foul, pointing immediately to the penalty spot, and MoM Young picked himself up, dusted himself down and hammered the spot kick into the back of the net for his second of the afternoon, helping his side to a 2-0 win.

The victory saw Broadbridge Heath move into one of the play-off places in seventh – just one point behind Hastings United.

Fixtures continue to come thick and fast with the Bears travelling to second-placed Erith Town on Tuesday evening before returning home again on Saturday to face leaders Faversham Town.

BBH: Hadfield, Thiselton, Royall, Marino (Church 65), Hyde (Peters 70), Richardson, Connell, Bejashvili (Rawlins 71), Buchanan, Hards (Doughty 90), Young.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, the Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was important that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

However, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

It has been revealed that the frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

Recent findings suggest that frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

According to recent reports, just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

In a recent development, the two-goal lead was very rapidly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

In the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

It was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

It has been revealed that amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

The change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

Not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

Sources indicate that there was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for tech giant, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

Sources indicate that milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

According to recent reports, with 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

Industry observers note that milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that roffey faced clear table toppers Haywards Heath, at the Fusion Aviation Stadium on Saturday, determined to gain revenge for the narrow, and perhaps undeserved, loss at Hanbury Park earlier in the season. However, in the end, despite having 14 attempts on goal with 6 on target, it was the visitors who took the points with two clinical finishes from their four on target efforts and two off target.

In the second minute Jordan Mase went down the left then cut in and switched the ball across the box to Luke Harrison whose shot took a slight deflection, taking the pace off it and Ethan McGrath in the Blues goal saved. In the fourth minute Mase again advanced before squaring it, this time to Stan Berry who hit a fierce drive just past the right-hand post, with McGrath probably covering it. Two minutes later Tom Caplin fed Moyo on the right and after his first cross was blocked at the near post he found Caplin 12 yards out but his shot although right in the corner, lacked the pace to beat McGrath.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Boars continued to dominate possession and after a quarter of an hour, Mase set the ball back for Charlie Gibson to fire over from twenty yards. Next a Gibson corner was deflected up in the air by a defender and Pat Gibs headed it back into the danger area where Berry controlled the ball in the air before hitting a spectacular bicycle shot a foot over the bar. Gibson hit his hot wide at the end of quick break and Berry hit the side netting after good work from Harrison and Callum Kilkenny.

Recent findings suggest that heath had their first attempt on goal after twenty-two minutes when Sonny Causton was played through, but with defenders converging, hit his shot from the edge of the box straight at Charlie Burton. Back came Roffey and Teddy Wood put a twenty yarder narrowly past the right-hand post. Heath responded with Mark Goldson getting behind the defence, but Pat Gibbs held him up and the Boars got men back with his attempt ending tamely in Burton’s arms. Goldson had another chance when the ball was switched from the right, but he sliced his shot wide.

The breakthrough came on thirty-three minutes when a Roffey attack broke down, and the ball was quickly transferred to Josh Wright who had kept himself onside. Burton advanced to push him wide but Callum Kilkenny who had sprinted back went over the top of the outstretched keeper and Wright managed to squeeze the ball in at the far post despite the desperate efforts of Jack Meeres on the line. Wood replied with a shot that was saved comfortably by McGrath. After all that action the half ended quietly with the visitors having the advantage.

Roffey had the first attempt on goal after the break with Moyo’s shot being taken above his head by McGrath. The game became much more contained with Heath happy to close Roffey down and maintain their lead. The next significant action didn’t come until thirteen minutes before time when Roffey lost possession in their own area but forced Harry Shooman to shoot over. Roffey were still very much in the game, but this changed on eighty minutes as they threw men forward, the hosts were caught on the break and Wright held off Meeres and rolled the ball past Burton to double the lead. Roffey wouldn’t give up but Heath were now able to sit back and soak up the pressure. Gibsons free kick hit the wall and deflected for a corner which was cleared. As stoppage time approached the Boars had a great chance to stay in the game when Caplin spread the play out to Harrison whose cross picked out the same player, unmarked ten yards out, but he scuffed his shot and McGrath saved. There was still time for Moyo to force a save out of McGrath at the near post and the same player hit a shot wide but unfortunately time had run out for the Boars. The table toppers had shown a clinical edge and managed their way to the three points.

Roffey are still very much in the fight for a top five place and it looks like that could be between eight or nine teams and the Boars next match is away to one of them, Hassocks who sit two places above the Boars, on December 1st.

Industry observers note that roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Gibbs(Moyo), Meeres, Wood, Mase, Berry(Allen), Caplin, Kilkenny(Hoarty). Subs: Pearse, Skerry.

Paris Saint-Germain vs Roma - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.
  • Double Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain will look to continue their stroll through this season's league phase, when they welcome Roma to Parc des Princes on Wednesday evening.
  • The competition's top scorers, peerless PSG have claimed maximum points, while their Italian visitors have spectacularly thrown several away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Double Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain will look to continue their stroll through this season's league phase, when they welcome Roma to Parc des Princes on Wednesday evening.

The competition's top scorers, peerless PSG have claimed maximum points, while their Italian visitors have spectacularly thrown several away.

Having kicked off their second title defence with an emphatic 6-1 win over Slovan Bratislava, PSG then posted consecutive 4-2 victories against Manchester City and Barcelona.

Usually sluggish starters in the league phase, Luis Enrique's men then stepped up another gear by smashing six past Villarreal without reply, ruthlessly maintaining their perfect record.

Already out of sight within 16 minutes and two seconds, PSG set a new fastest time to score four goals in a Champions League match, before slightly easing off the gas.

Furthermore, a tally of 20 goals is the most by any club from their first four group or league phase fixtures, and Barca's overall best of 28 is now under serious threat.

Also unbeaten in 14 games at Europe's elite level, Les Parisiens can surpass Lyon's French record by at least avoiding defeat in midweek.

Despite losing Desire Doue to a serious injury, PSG still beat Nice 3-2 on Saturday night, recording their 12th consecutive win across all competitions.

Now leading city rivals Paris FC by three points at the top of the Ligue 1 table, they are well set to sweep all before them again.

Ahead of their first competitive meeting with PSG - a prospect to be feared and savoured in equal measure - Roma warmed up with a 5-1 win over Parma at the weekend.

Staying within two points of surprise Serie A leaders Lazio - their loathed city rivals - the Giallorossi inched ahead of Scudetto holders Inter Milan, largely thanks to a four-goal haul for Donyell Malen.

After another stellar display at Stadio Tardini, Malen has racked up 26 league goals in 2026, while Roma have already fired home 36 this season.

That is more than any other team at this stage of an Italian top-flight campaign since 1950, and Gian Piero Gasperini's side also remain unbeaten.

However, in the Champions League they have effectively let eight points slip, following a late collapse at home to Real Madrid and their substantial blow-up at Old Trafford earlier this month.

Roma somehow squandered a two-goal lead to lose against Manchester United on matchday four, leaving them 20th in the Champions League standings and at risk of early elimination.

Now bound for France to face the toughest test of all, the Giallorossi have won just one of their last 11 away games in UEFA's top competition, while conceding in all of the last 33.

Paris Saint-Germain Champions League form:.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Further diminishing PSG's talented front line, Doue must join Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the long road to recovery from an ACL injury.

More positively for Luis Enrique - a former Roma coach - Ousmane Dembele recently made his comeback from a layoff.

Fabian Ruiz has posted goal involvements in all of his last four Champions League appearances, scoring in the last two, and he should start in central midfield.

Club captain Marquinhos moved to Paris from Roma in 2013, while reserve left-back Lucas Digne spent the 2015-16 campaign on loan with the Giallorossi.

Roma welcomed back Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar during the international break, but Lorenzo Pellegrini is still unavailable.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Leonardo Balerdi (ankle) are both struggling to recover in time for Wednesday's game.

Brazilian wing-back Wesley notched a hat-trick of assists in Parma, despite only appearing as a second-half substitute, so he will expect to play at Parc des Princes.

A sure starter up front, Malen now tops the Capocannoniere rankings with 12 Serie A goals, having recently scored in the Nations League and found the net in three consecutive Champions League matches.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Mayulu.

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen.

PSG's latest injury setback will surely have an impact, but the goals and points should keep flowing on Wednesday.

While Gasperini's Roma are often a delight to behold, their defence can be caught out at the very top level, so they will leave Paris empty-handed.

Eastbourne United and Guernsey show why they are promotion contenders

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (571 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 4-1 defeat left Guernsey smarting and United in a very good position in second place in the SCFL Premier.
  • Since then, the Green Lions have been on an unbeaten run, making themselves genuine play-off contenders along with United.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 4-1 defeat left Guernsey smarting and United in a very good position in second place in the SCFL Premier.

Since then, the Green Lions have been on an unbeaten run, making themselves genuine play-off contenders along with United. It was obvious from the moment they arrived at the Oval that they would only be happy with all three points, preferably by at least the same scoreline.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The early encounters went to United, and with just seven minutes on the clock James Jull shot home, only for the linesman to raise his flag for offside to howls of derision from the home support.

Guernsey started to make their mark with a couple of runs from Charlton Gauvain, but the visitors also left their mark on United’s players, collecting two yellow cards.

Hull went very close with an acrobatic scissor kick, and Joe Overy continued to needle away down the left wing, Charlie Ball forcing the keeper into a good save from one of Overy’s low crosses.

In first half added time, Guernsey took the lead with a fine shot from range beating Alieu Secka.

United were unperturbed and Rhyle Ovenden was unfortunate not to even it up straight after the break, his free kick just scraping the top of the crossbar.

On the hour Hull was replaced by Callum Barlow, before the increasingly confident Ovenden had a shot well saved by the Lions keeper.

In a recent development, five minutes later, Barlow’s lightning-fast cross found Overy, who turned and slotted home well for 1-1. Overy rarely misses an attempt in the area, and Guernsey looked crestfallen.

There was a third and a fourth yellow card for Guernsey, who were pondering returning with only a point, when Ball broke past the defences and slotted home with an inch perfect side foot to make it 2-1 to United to the joy of the crowd, and despair of the islanders.

Rather than crumble, it galvanised Guernsey, and the United lead only lasted four minutes as Gauvain made it 2-2. Now it was a real blood and thunder contest, both teams showing exactly why they are in the top four, Secka made a wonderful save to keep it equal, Ball and Barlow both trying out the away keeper, but it remained 2-2.

After months out injured, the home crowd were delighted to see – on 85 minutes – Mason Creese come on, replacing Ball, and Freddie Jones took up position on the other flank replacing Overy.

Both added even more pace, and despite the cold, the crowd were heating up – while Guernsey overheated as they collected a fifth yellow in what was never a nasty encounter. As the final whistle went both teams were treated to an ovation as they left the field. This is the sort of fare non-league crowds absolutely love - hard tackling, fast attacking, stout defending and not a player from either side faking injury to get an opponent booked.

Both teams should be in the play-offs - one of them could be champions, time will tell.

Next up for United, this Saturday, is a home game with an improving Forest Row, who will be desperate for the points to help them out of the drop zone. It’s a 3pm kick-off at the Oval.

Fabian Hurzeler's side - who remain second in the table - suffered a 2-0 loss at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, with Oli McBurnie scoring twice in stoppage time after Albion missed chances to take control.

Brighton were frustrated after failing to make their first-half dominance count, but midfielder Andres is looking ahead to the visit of Romanian league leaders Universitatea Craiova in the Uefa Conference League.

Sources indicate that the Spaniard has made an impressive impact since his £18m summer arrival, featuring 10 times for Albion in all competitions, including eight Premier League appearances. He has also scored and provided an assist.

Andres believes the squad must learn from the setback at Hull rather than allow it to affect their confidence.

“What is good for us, we have another game on Thursday,” he said.

“We're already focused on that, and I think we need to focus on ourselves, keep training, see what we did wrong today, learn, and of course go again because this is football and sometimes you lose.

“I think the team spirit and team effort is not going to go down, so we will come back again.”.

The 21-year-old acknowledged the cost of Brighton's missed chances against a Hull side who showed their quality late on.

Industry observers note that “This is the Premier League, no? If you don't use the chances you have, and then you give this kind of team the opportunity to beat you, that is what they got.”.

Andres added that Albion must accept the defeat, learn from it and move forward promptly.

Thursday's meeting with Craiova offers an immediate opportunity for Brighton to respond.

“We will recover from this and bounce back again,” he remarked.

Brighton then return to Premier League action this Sunday against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium.

  • Two teams that have struggled during the league stage of the 2026-27 Champions League will lock horns on Wednesday, as Slavia Prague welcome Villarreal.
  • The two sides previously went to battle in the 2017-18 Europa League group stage, with the corresponding clash in that campaign finishing 2-0 to Villarreal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 17:36, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:42.

Two teams that have struggled during the league stage of the 2026-27 Champions League will lock horns on Wednesday, as Slavia Prague welcome Villarreal.

The two sides previously went to battle in the 2017-18 Europa League group stage, with the corresponding clash in that campaign finishing 2-0 to Villarreal.

Slavia Prague boast a record of zero wins, one draw and three defeats from their four matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League, with one point leaving them down in 34th spot in the table.

The Red and Whites opened their Champions League league stage campaign with a 3-2 defeat to Lens, before going down 2-0 to Sabah, but they managed to pick up their first point on October 20, drawing 2-2 with Fenerbahce.

Jindrich Trpisovsky's side can also take plenty of positives from their performance against Arsenal in the competition last time out, going down 2-1 to the Gunners.

Slavia Prague will enter this match off the back of successive league wins over Artis Brno and Sigma Olomouc, with the results leaving them top of their domestic table, boasting 37 points from their first 15 games of the campaign.

The Red and Whites have only been victorious in one of their previous 13 matches against Spanish opposition, losing six times in the process, and they have never actually managed to beat a Spanish club in the Champions League proper.

Villarreal, meanwhile, are unbeaten in their nine previous matches against Czech clubs, recording six wins in the process; the Yellow Submarine have also been victorious in three of their five games in Czechia, including the last two.

The La Liga club finished 35th in last season's league stage, so there is huge room for improvement this term, but it has been another difficult European campaign to date.

Inigo Perez's side opened their league stage campaign with a 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund, before recording a 3-1 win over Napoli, but they have lost their last two in the competition against Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain.

Villarreal have three points from their four matches in this season's league stage, which has left them down in 28th spot in the table.

The Yellow Submarine will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 defeat to Barcelona, with the result leaving them 10th in the La Liga table.

Slavia Prague will be without the services of Stepan Chaloupek (hamstring), David Moses (muscular), Adonija Ouanda (muscular), Elias Pitak (ankle) and Danijel Sturm (muscular) due to injury problems.

Meanwhile, Lukas Provod (tendon) needs to be assessed before a final decision is made on his involvement in the Champions League fixture.

Wiktor Nowak and Mojmir Chytil have netted seven times each for Slavia Prague this season, and the pair are both expected to be in the starting side.

As for Villarreal, Ilias Akhomach (muscular), Alassane Diatta (hamstring), Juan Foyth (muscular) and Gerard Moreno (muscular) are absent due to injury problems.

Georges Mikautadze has scored five goals and registered two assists in 18 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season, and the 26-year-old will feature in the final third.

There is also expected to be a spot in the starting side for Tani Oluwaseyi, who has four goals and one assist in 13 appearances during the current campaign.

Markovic; Holes, Zima, N’Guessan; Vlcek, Sadilek, Nowak, Jurasek; Ayaosi, Suleiman; Chytil.

Villarreal possible starting lineup:.

Gulacsi; Mourino, L Costa, Veiga, Romero; Saliba, Gueye; Buchanan, Moleiro, Oluwaseyi; Mikautadze.

Both teams have struggled in Europe this season, and we are finding it difficult to separate them in this contest, ultimately backing a 1-1 draw.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roy Keane remarked Brighton’s “sloppy” finishing cost them dearly but gave all the credit to Hull City's determination after they stunned the Seagulls with two late goals to claim a 2-0 Premier League victory.

The Seagulls looked the better side for much of Sunday's contest, creating numerous opportunities but failing to find a way past an inspired Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Brighton were made to pay for their wastefulness when Oli McBurnie struck twice in stoppage time, following Costinha's late dismissal for a second yellow card.

And former Manchester United captain Keane believes Hull deserve enormous credit for their fighting spirit after sustained pressure from Albion.

"It's a mad game. The sending off had a major impact. Brighton were desperately trying to win the game, and you have to give credit to them, but they left spaces and gaps," Keane told Sky Sports.

"It's brilliant from Hull, great fighting spirit and a bit of quality. Great composure from McBurnie. You think McBurnie has missed the opportunity, but what a huge goal.".

Keane was also keen to highlight the contribution of Hull goalkeeper Tzolakis, who produced a string of outstanding saves to frustrate Fabian Hurzeler's side.

"Instead of being critical of Brighton, you have to give credit to the goalkeeper," he added.

"They might not have Brighton's quality, but they demonstrated great fighting spirit, composure, and stayed in the game; you have to give them huge credit for that.".

The result leaves Brighton second in the Premier League table with 22 points from 11 matches, while Hull climb to 11th with 14 points.

Albion will look to respond when they welcome Newcastle United to the Amex Stadium on Sunday, November 29 (2.05pm).

Hull, meanwhile, travel to Crystal Palace on the same afternoon as they look to build on an impressive victory.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW.

Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger).

The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25.

'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'.

Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

'It's devastating,' said Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

Sources indicate that 'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just remarked to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

Industry observers note that 'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

Recent findings suggest that 'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'.

Holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

Sources indicate that 'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

According to recent reports, 'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'.

Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway remarked on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'.

O’Neill admits this could be an option for Celtic if he chooses to play a system that he once was synonymous with during his first spell in charge at the club.

“Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it,” noted O’Neill. “He competes better in the air than I ever thought he did.

According to recent reports, “It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that. He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.”.

In a recent development, celtic face a tough upcoming run of games, including travelling to take on second-tier Portuguese club Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday night. Two more away games against Hearts and Dundee quickly follow. The Parkhead side have just one more home match – against St Johnstone – before Christmas. Two other assignments, against Aberdeen and Omonia Nicosia, are away.

O’Neill has already spoken of “manoeuvring” players in the first-team squad to ensure no one is pushed beyond their limits.

Tierney clearly merits the most concern given his injury history. However, he has been quietly putting in the minutes for his club as well as his country in recent weeks. He has played the full 90 minutes of two of Celtic’s last four matches and was only subbed off on Saturday with 20 minutes left against St Mirren with the game already won. O’Neill revealed that he has a crafty tactic for dealing with the player if he begins to look like he might want to come off; he pretends not to notice him. There is no point in the player looking forlornly towards the dugout.

“Tierney played two 90 minutes for Scotland and that made it difficult for him to last the full game against St Mirren,” said O'Neill.

“Internationals take it out of you and he played every second. He played left centre back and that maybe means less running, but those games are tough.

“Previous to his injury, he was feeling it. But since he’s been back, he’s played a lot of games. Sometimes with Kieran, when you feel as if he’s flagging, you just ignore him. If he’s coming near you, you turn away because you want him to play the games!

“Kieran has done great for me,” he added. "He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too. Kieran will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

Industry observers note that “Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal. He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too.

According to recent reports, “I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about Kieran. He’s a great lad too - very popular in the dressing room.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alfred Johansson insists Motherwell’s latest accounts show the club are trending upwards - with Norway’s Bodo Glimt a key reference point.

The Premiership side have reported a profit of £2.3M, which rises to £3.1M when excluding depreciation and finance costs, for the 2025/26 financial year. A record of £5M was generated from player trading while former manager Jens Berthel Askou achieved a fourth place finish in last term’s top flight.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In a recent development, current manager Johansson’s work was largely in Scandinavia before travelling to Motherwell. He watched Bodo’s rise from lowly divisions to Champions League competitors and feels that reveals what a step-by-step approach can do for a club’s long term aspirations. Former Rosenborg gaffer Johansson said: “I can't really use that to ask for more time in terms of performing but definitely, it's evidence of what the club has been doing for the past 18 months at least, that it’s something that is working.

Industry observers note that “So that alignment in the club, that philosophy, and that strategy, like we do things like this, and the connection I feel between people inside here and the offices, that everyone wants to pull together in that direction. That is what gives you output all the time.

Industry observers note that “This is a club that the budget is very small compared with some of the teams that we want to compete with. That was the same for Bodo/Glimt 10 years ago. Their budget was so small, they went down to the 2nd division in Norway, now they are playing Champions League. You have to build stone by stone, and that's what Motherwell are trying to do, and that's what I feel every day inside these walls.”.

Industry observers note that motherwell’s long-term goals are also set to be boosted by a training base being built at nearby Dalziel Park where they at the moment undergo preparation for matches. Johansson is keen to see the club build on its ability to grasp marginal gains. He explained: ”You don't have that much time in football nowadays. I get asked in the press conference about patience and everything is related to time.

According to recent reports, “That means that you have to make the most out of your time. Maybe before 30 years ago you had to optimise every week. Now you have to optimise every hour in top football. That's down to recovery of players, work with their bodies, and you need facilities to be able to facilitate that work. So that's one part of it.

Recent findings suggest that “That you need to add the facilities for the players to be able to do the work that's needed to play every few days and with that intensity that. Now I saw that from all the top leagues in Europe, that the Scottish Premiership was the second in the world in explosive accelerations, for instance.

“That's one of the more demanding things that you can put the body through. So you need to be able to react. You need to recover from that between matches and trainings, and so on. So you need the facilities for that. We don't have that much time. Right now we are driving back and forth to Dalziel Park. I could maybe take five minutes in my office with a player or on the pitch talking to a player. All of this is optimising time and I think it's essential today.”.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley spoke last week of the lack of national performance centre in Scotland, like Sweden are building in Johansson’s homeland. He added: “I definitely see the point of that's needed. I mean, Denmark, they've been working also now for some years.

“They have a strategy now in place for how to build that centre, Sweden the same. Uh, we know that other countries, they did it 20 years ago, like like the Belgians and the Portuguese FA, they did it. They built a fresh facility after the Euros. So, of course, it's there to push things and it's needed.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton should have right-back Joao Costinha available for Thursday's Uefa Conference League clash despite his late dismissal against Hull City.

The Portuguese defender was sent off in the 89th minute of Sunday's 2-0 Premier League defeat at the MKM Stadium after receiving a second yellow card for his foul on Sorba Thomas.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The dismissal proved costly for Fabian Hurzeler's second placed side, who conceded twice in stoppage time through Oli McBurnie.

However, Costinha will escape a European suspension because his red card was received in a domestic competition.

Under FA rules, receiving a second caution in the same match carries an automatic one-game suspension, which only kicks in for the domestic league and domestic cups.

That means Costinha will miss this Sunday’s match Premier League clash against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium but should be available for Albion’s trip to Bournemouth on December 2.

Uefa operates separately to the Premier League which means Costinha can feature against Universitatea Craiova at the Amex Stadium on Thursday.

Hurzeler admitted the sending-off had a significant impact on Brighton's defeat but insisted the referee was not responsible for the result.

"Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role," he said.

The German added: "For 65 minutes we indicated a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards.

In a recent development, "In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going.".

Hurzeler also refused to blame referee Peter Bankes, saying: "The referee wasn't the reason why we lost.".
