On his debut, the 54-year-old boss has already set two unwanted records in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool on Sunday. Pochettino is the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his first match in charge of a club. United are just one point ahead of bottom club Crystal Palace. It is hard to know whether the answer will come through the January window, but the United hierarchy could think so.

Evanilson, 27, has scored eight goals and provided five assists in 15 games this season. He said: ‘Here in England, among the substantial clubs, Manchester United are the team I like most. Rayan said the same. When I was a kid, I used to watch United too. When Cristiano Ronaldo played there, I watched loads of his highlights. And, man, knowing that I am here playing against them... This is my third season playing against them. I scored last season and I scored this season at Old Trafford. It is a dream, and I say it to everyone in interviews: it was a dream to play in that stadium, and scoring goals is even more important. So it is a dream I am fulfilling, scoring a goal against United because of the greatness of the club.’.

According to recent reports, with a contract until June 2029, Evanilson is unlikely to leave Bournemouth in the middle of the season. The club, fifth in the table, probably have no intention of letting their number nine go, as he is their top scorer and assist provider in the Premier League. The chance of securing European football could encourage Bournemouth to ignore any offer from United.

For their part, there is no specific rumour suggesting United are interested in the forward, but the club’s poor sporting situation opens the door to a larger recruitment drive in January. With striker Benjamin Sesko injured, United are thinking about Pio Esposito, who is in great form for Inter Milan. And why not try Evanilson, who is already a fan of the Red Devils and could well be tempted by the prospect of moving despite everything?

Just as Peretz's brilliant save from Tahith Chong was undone by Sydie Peck beating him in the 90th minute, so it looked like the midfielder's 90th-minute goal and Jordan Ayew's brilliance to create it might have been in vain when Finn Azaz played Samuel Edozie through in stoppage time.

But Cooper came out on top in the one-on-one to earn his side a 1-1 draw against opponents who completely outplayed the Blades in the first half-hour.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

If only they had played the first half as they had the second, perhaps they might have been celebrating victory rather than a point which felt like one, thanks to the timing of Peck's goal.

If the first half revealed how short the Blades are of the very best in the division, the second showed what they have in their locker to try to do something about it.

Southampton will have walked off more relieved to take the point than the home team.

The Saints took the lead in the 11th minute when Hamza Choudhury gave the ball away and was unable to close Lewis Dobbin down before he curled a beautiful shot inside the far post.

Already by then it was on the cards, with Saints dominating possession as James Ward-Prowse pulled the strings in midfield.

The only saving grace is that the Blades only trailed 1-0 at the break.

Mads Roerslev had a shot blocked and Kuryu Matsuki thrashed an effort into the side netting from a tight angle.

The Blades did at least improve as half-time approached, Mark McGuinness heading a Peck corner, and Romelle Donovan - switched to the right - came inside and shot at the goalkeeper.

With Patrick Bamford introduced at the break, the Blades were much sharper in the second half.

Peck's shot from distance in the 50th minute revealed ambition, if not accuracy.

A couple of minutes later, Bamford headed over at a corner nodded to him by Mark McGuinness. Next was Ayew, who headed at Daniel Peterz after Donovan got to the byline to tee the chance up.

Ayew was released down the left but delayed too long, and could only force a corner from a tight angle.

Donovan had a penalty appeal waved away, perhaps not helped by the fact he was clearly looking for it.

But the football was as one-way as the first half had been, only with more chances to show from it.

Chong was unable to keep his shot down when the ball dropped to him 16 yards out, and Harrison Burrows had an effort blocked.

Southampton briefly provided some variety in the 80th minute when Donovan blocked Cyle Larin and Ward-Prowse ballooned the follow-up over, but the play promptly moved back to the Kop End.

Chong's cross went all the way through to Burrows at the back post, but he could only loop his header up for Peretz to catch.

In a recent development, but the gilt-edged chance fell to Chong in the 83rd after a lovely move through Ayes and Bamford. The winger steered his shot into the right place, but Peretz stretched out brilliantly to his right to save it.

When that was squandered, it felt like the Blades might run out of time.

But in the 90th minute Ayew did brilliantly to dribble along the byline and pull the ball back for Peck to find the net through a busy penalty area.

It could have counted for nought had Cooper not intervened in the 95th minute.

As saves go, it was a pretty massive one.

Latest Update: How the Dylan Tombides Foundation is educating footballers about testicular cancer

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 15 years ago, a random drugs test at the Under-17 World Cup revealed that West Ham striker and Australian youth international Dylan Tombides had testicular cancer.
  • Originally misdiagnosed by his GP as a cyst, Tombides’ mother, Tracy, and brother, Taylor, are now on a mission to minimise the likelihood of such a mistake happening again by getting people to know what to look for.
  • Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in males aged 15 to 44, but highly treatable and in most cases curable when detected early - so education is key to saving lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

15 years ago, a random drugs test at the Under-17 World Cup revealed that West Ham striker and Australian youth international Dylan Tombides had testicular cancer. He would pass away three years later at the age of 20.

Originally misdiagnosed by his GP as a cyst, Tombides’ mother, Tracy, and brother, Taylor, are now on a mission to minimise the likelihood of such a mistake happening again by getting people to know what to look for.

Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in males aged 15 to 44, but highly treatable and in most cases curable when detected early - so education is key to saving lives.

That is why the DT38 Foundation was set up in Dylan’s name and why Tracy and Taylor, in partnership with FIFA Medical, are explaining to players at this year’s U17 World Cup in Doha why regular self-examination matters and how to carry it out.

“Getting the call from FIFA was a massive opportunity and an amazing thing for us and for the charity,” Taylor tells Standard Sport.

Recent findings suggest that “Obviously, it’s where Dylan last kind of played healthy before his diagnosis. So to come back to where it all started for us as a family is a grateful honour.”.

£75m Chelsea star ‘considered retirement’ under Maresca.

Fernandes fumes in unseen interview amid newly introduced Man Utd red card verdict.

Chelsea injury enhancement: Caicedo, Joao Pedro, James latest return dates.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

Tracy and Taylor have spoken to more than 1,200 players across the tournament, and their story has really hit home.

In a recent development, “One of the young players stood in front of me and stated, ‘I’m so sorry for your loss. I’m sorry your son isn’t coming home to you. We are so grateful that you are telling us all about it’,” Tracy claims.

“(We are) very grateful to have this opportunity to educate 1,200 players out here this fortnight, that hopefully will go home and pass on the message of the signs and symptoms of testicular cancer and the importance of an ultrasound scan.”.

The DT38 foundation have a campaign called ‘Check One Two’, encouraging men to check themselves on the first day of every month.

Dylan’s nickname - ‘Didge’ - also provides an acronym and hashtag for the foundation: Delay Is Deadly, Get Educated.

FIFA medical director Andy Massey has worked with the DT38 Foundation to get Tracy and Taylor talking to players at the U17 World Cup and notes it is an initiative that he hopes to continue year on year.

“What I would love to do is carry this on next year for the Under-17s,” Massey claims.

Sources indicate that “It’s an annual event now (the World Cup) for Under-17s. We’re going to be in the same place until 2029, and it would be fantastic to do it (talk to players) again for next year and the year after.”.

We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it.

Massey continued by underlining the value of the work Tracy and Taylor are doing, with free scans now on offer to players during the tournament.

In a recent development, “We don’t want this to be a box-ticking exercise. We don’t want this to be a, ‘Let’s pat ourselves on the back, we’re working for a charity’.

“This is one of the biggest things that I think I’ve ever done in my sports medicine career because it has such a reach.”.

The DT38 Foundation are starting with the U17 World Cup, but ultimately Taylor hopes their work will have an impact down the generations.

It has been revealed that “The effect is lasting,” he indicates. “If we can teach these kids now, we know the next generation, they’ll teach their kids and they’ll teach their kids and it’ll be continuous.

It has been revealed that “We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it. Without FIFA, we couldn’t touch as many people as we have.”.

Visit dt38.org to find out more about the DT38 Foundation, Dylan's story and advice and guidance about testicular cancer.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.
  • The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the issue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 23 November 2026.

Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.

The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the issue.

Celtic will receive 508 tickets for the Premiership encounter on November 29, which will be their first visit to Tynecastle since beating Hearts to the title in the final stages of last season, a victory which resulted in a pitch invasion from some of their fans at Celtic Park.

A Celtic statement read: 'As supporters will know, our allocation for our forthcoming match against Heart of Midlothian at Tynecastle Stadium has been cut by 20 per cent, compared to our previous visit.

'There have been a variety of views expressed to the club from supporters in relation to accepting this allocation. Some groups representing travelling supporters explained to the club that their members did not wish to accept the tickets because of the reduced allocation.

'We have taken that into consideration and also raised their concerns with the home club, who have assured us that they have spoken to Police Scotland.

Hearts had stated that only 508 tickets will be made available for Celtic fans on November 29.

'Having carefully considered all of the circumstances, we can confirm we will accept the allocation of 508 tickets.

'We respect all views and opinions on this matter, and while we are concerned and disappointed at this reduction, and others across recent years, we feel it is important that the team has the backing of our fans within the stadium for an important match.

'We realise the difficulties such a reduction can cause and in light of our discussions with supporters, we can confirm that should any supporter who is successful in the ballot, but does not wish to accept this ticket, then this will NOT affect the away ticket record moving forward.

'We thank our fans for their continued support and can confirm that we will be discussing the matter further with both the home club and the SPFL.'.

Celtic and Rangers formerly received the full Roseburn Stand for their supporters at Tynecastle, which resulted in an allocation of almost 3,500 tickets.

However, that figure was reduced to about 1,250 tickets in the 2021-22 season amid increased demand from home fans after the lockdown, and was further cut by about half.

Only Hibernian now get the full Roseburn Stand in a reciprocal agreement between the Edinburgh rivals.

Tynecastle has a capacity of about 20,000 but Hearts’ attendances are normally around 18,700 as a number of seats are not in use to create a barrier between the home and away fans.

Visiting clubs get about 800 tickets for games at Celtic Park, which has a 60,000 capacity.

#107085. How Noni Madueke grew into a unique piece at Arsenal amid injury absences

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1136 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

How Noni Madueke grew into a unique piece at Arsenal amid injury absences

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.
  • Noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game.
  • A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.

Noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game. Signed from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing, and he had to justify an investment in a player who initially appeared destined to be a back-up.

A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke received a longer run of opportunities and took the space. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of that growth.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In his press conference, the boss highlighted the variety the forward has added to the game and his involvement without the ball.

Madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives in one-on-one situations.

That characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In 2024-25, he was one of the Premier League players who progressed the ball towards the box the most and created danger mainly through individual carries. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

In a recent development, ‘He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forwards,’ Arteta said. ‘And he is doing it in various ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and much more connection to his game.’.

According to recent reports, the numbers help show the scale of the growth. According to FotMob’s Premier League 2026-27 data, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, against 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although Saka has played fewer minutes. The growth also shows in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

‘And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball,’ Arteta remarked. ‘So I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying that a lot.’.

The development is therefore not about abandoning the dribble, but knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, but now seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

Comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right and move inside, but they do it in different ways. Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and moves naturally between carries, short passes and crosses. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal’s main attacking tools.

Recent findings suggest that madueke offers more explosion in the first movement and tends to seek one-on-one duels more often. He is more vertical, liking to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When confident, he can disorganise a defence without relying on a long build-up.

The creation data help illustrate the difference. As well as beating Saka for chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob’s numbers, Madueke also demonstrates a higher volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps an advantage in shooting and defensive involvement. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

Sources indicate that that difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka may be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that breaks down the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating individual imbalances.

The Englishman has also shown he can play on the left, a role he took on when Christos Tzolis was absent. There he must adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can go to the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta’s options and stops the team depending on a single alternative for each side.

According to recent reports, the competition with Saka does not need to be seen as an attempt to remove the starter. Arsenal need more than one player able to decide matches, especially in a long season with the Premier League, Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is beginning to offer arguments to be considered more than simple cover.

In a recent development, one detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Arteta highlighted the player’s reaction as an example to the rest of the squad. The boss said Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

According to recent reports, ‘He went to train and came back a different Noni,’ Arteta explained. ‘He was not willing to accept that situation and showed he was determined. Since then, it has been incredible.’.

The individual work did not start now, however. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has worked for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention on being more decisive in the final third.

The result has shown in the numbers: his average of chances created more than doubled compared with the previous season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate rose from 50 per cent to 55 per cent, while his pass accuracy went from 78 per cent to 87 per cent. In open-play crosses, his success rate jumped from 14 per cent to 33 per cent.

According to recent reports, those numbers help explain why Arteta speaks of a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but has begun to execute other actions better, which could previously limit his influence. The growth combined different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

Roberto De Zerbi has cast doubt on his future, four months into his first full season at Tottenham Hotspur.

After arriving in March, the 47-year-old has presided over a summer window which has seen the likes of Sandro Tonali, Andrew Robertson and Savio touch down in north London.

But De Zerbi, whose contract with Spurs runs until 2031, has admitted doubts over his long-term future in the game.

The Italian told Canal+: “I don’t think I’ll stay in football much longer. Your life revolves around football, but life isn’t just that.

“That time hasn’t come yet. For me, being a coach at this level is already a dream.”.

After enduring a tough start to the 2026/27 Premier League season, Spurs have won four of their last five fixtures, most recently beating Ipswich 2-0.

Before arriving at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, De Zerbi spent time in Ligue 1 with nine-time champions Marseille after leaving Brighton and Hove Albion, but a 5-0 hammering by rivals PSG saw the Italian depart in February of this year.

The Italian joined Spurs shortly thereafter with the club one point away from a first relegation since 1977, and clinched Premier League survival with final-day delight against David Moyes’ Everton.

Currently sat in 10th place, De Zerbi’s Spurs are targeting a weekend victory against relegation-threatened Sunderland to continue a run of good form, but the manager has his eyes set on more.

He said: “I don’t measure dreams by the titles won, but more by the human impact you have.

Recent findings suggest that “I always want to stay the same, always look people in the eye. Even when I make mistakes, because I make a lot of them.”.

What position do you prefer to play?

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

You’re Milan’s top scorer. Will we see a bicycle kick soon?

Evanilson scored the pick of the goals, firing home from an audacious angle after rounding Senne Lammens.

The former FC Porto man shared that his favourite club in England is Manchester United - sharing a soft spot for the Red Devils with his fellow countryman, exciting winger Rayan.

Industry observers note that evanilson told Globo Esporte: “So I joke around with Rayan. I think that, here in England, of the big clubs, United are the team I like the most. Rayan mentioned the same thing. When I was a kid, I also used to watch United.”.

Sources indicate that “When Cristiano Ronaldo played for United, I watched loads of his highlights. And, man, knowing that I’m here playing against them….

“This is my third season playing against them. I scored last season and I scored this season at Old Trafford.

“It’s a dream, and I tell everyone this in interviews: it was a dream to play at that stadium, and scoring goals is even more vital.
